text: When an ECP5 matmul array exceeds the 48-DSP budget and its 57.2 MHz path is FF->MULT18X18D->32-bit carry chain, shrink to 6x8=48 PEs, cut accumulation to 24 bits, and set dsp_regs=in_pipe_out with pipe_mul=1 and reg_in=true to register the multiplier output and array inputs, removing the DSP-to-carry and IO-to-array routes from the critical path and raising Fmax to 170.1 MHz (+112.9 MHz) while cutting 2369 LUTs.

When an ECP5 matmul's 24-bit accumulator carry chain is congestion-inflated at 48 PEs (2.69 ns route, 170.1 MHz), cut the array to 4x8=32 PEs so the placer packs each chain tightly, dropping carry route to 1.84 ns and raising Fmax to 193.5 MHz (+23.5) while removing 1030 LUTs and 16 DSPs.

When an ECP5 matmul is feasible at 193.5 MHz with the critical path in the per-PE carry-chain route (1.84 ns) and plenty of DSP headroom, avoid adding columns from 8 to 10 for 40 MAC/cycle: it costs 8 DSPs and 562 LUTs and yields only +2 MHz (195.5 MHz) because the carry-chain route drops to 1.42 ns but the downstream LUT route rises from 0.88 to 1.17 ns, leaving total path nearly unchanged (5.17→5.12 ns).

When an ECP5 matmul is feasible at 195.5 MHz with the PE carry-chain accumulator critical path and only ~0.44 ns slack, do not add pe_cols from 10 to 12 to fill the 48-DSP budget; it costs +8 DSP and +564 LUT and drops Fmax to 188.5 MHz by stretching carry-chain route from 1.42 to 2.35 ns through wider-array column-route congestion.

When an ECP5 matmul PE is timing-limited at 76.6 MHz by a combinational MULT18X18D feeding a 32-bit carry-chain accumulator, collapse the 4×4 PE array to 1×1, set dsp_regs=in_pipe_out, pipe_mul=1, reg_in=true, and acc_width=24, which registers the multiplier output and shortens the carry chain, raising Fmax to 216.8 MHz while dropping LUTs from 1489 to 83 and DSPs from 16 to 1.

When scaling an ECP5 matmul from a 1x1 PE (1 DSP, 216.8 MHz) to a 4x8 PE array for 32 MACs/cycle, the 24-bit accumulator carry chain widens from 15 to 21 cells (route 1.63->1.79 ns) and the acc drain LUT route rises from 0.75 to 1.31 ns, costing 35.7 MHz (to 181.1 MHz), so use the 4x8 shape only if that Fmax still clears the 160 MHz target and keep the drain mux minimal.

When an ECP5 matmul at the 32-DSP cap is Fmax-limited at 181 MHz by a 5.52 ns accumulate loop (24-bit carry-chain routing 1.79 ns plus acc LUT routing 1.31 ns), halve pe_rows from 4 to 2 and double pe_cols from 8 to 16 to keep 32 MACs, which collapses the drain mux (-186 LUTs) and shortens the carry/LUT routes (1.79→1.45 ns and 1.31→1.27 ns) for +13.3 MHz (194.4 MHz).

When an ECP5 32-DSP output-stationary matmul is timing-limited by the PE accumulator carry chain (prod_q -> 21-cell carry -> acc LUT, 1.53 ns logic + 1.45 ns route), collapsing the array from 2x16 to 1x32 shortens the chain to 18 cells but worsens carry routing to 1.68 ns, yielding only +5.2 MHz (194.4->199.6 MHz) for +404 LUTs, so do not treat single-row packing as a general carry-chain fix.

On ECP5 1x32 matmul at the 32-DSP ceiling, keep the multiply result flopped in fabric immediately after the multiplier when the 5.01 ns prod_q→24-bit carry-chain→acc path sets 199.6 MHz; moving that flop to the DSP P output made b_skew→u_mult (3.49 ns logic + 2.7 ns route) critical, dropping Fmax to 148.9 MHz and losing feasibility, so trim carry-chain routing instead.

When an ECP5 matmul is timing-limited by LUT-logic in the operand path (b_skew to u_mult, 6.71 ns), switch the DSPs to internal input pipeline registers (in_pipe_out) and remove the fabric input registers to bypass that logic and shift the critical path to the accumulator carry chain (4.67 ns), gaining 65.2 MHz (feasible at 214.2 MHz) at +1 LUT and no extra DSPs.

On an ECP5 matmul whose 1×32 PE array is timing-limited by the per-PE accumulator carry-chain self-loop (FF→24-bit carry→LUT4→FF, routing-dominated), reshape to 2×16 to cut LUTs by 404 but expect ~9.6 MHz lower Fmax (214.2→204.6 MHz) because the shorter 16-column span does not shorten the carry-chain return enough to offset the reintroduced drain mux.

On an ECP5 matmul whose 32-DSP array is limited by the per-PE accumulator carry-chain feedback, don't add a second multiplier-to-accumulator fabric pipeline stage by rebalancing 1×32 to 2×16 PEs (pipe_mul 1→2) to gain placer slack: it dropped Fmax from 204.6 to 193.7 MHz and added 404 LUTs with no DSP change, because the critical path stayed the accumulator FF→carry-chain→LUT4→FF feedback (5.16 ns).

When an ECP5 matmul MAC is combinational from a b_in FF through an unregistered MULT18X18D straight into a 32-bit carry chain (13.06 ns, 76.6 MHz), register the DSP in/out, enable the multiplier pipeline, add input registers, and cut the accumulator to 24 bits; this isolates the DSP→carry path and lifts Fmax to 181.1 MHz (+104.6 MHz) at 40 DSPs despite +1193 LUTs.

On ECP5 matmul at 40 DSP, when the 24-bit per-PE accumulate carry chain is the critical path (2.12 ns route in a 5.52 ns/181.1 MHz path), reshape the PE grid from 5x8 to 4x10—same 40 DSP—to shorten the carry route to 1.8 ns and the path to 5.16 ns, raising Fmax to 193.8 MHz (+12.7 MHz) by reducing rows/drain-mux congestion while leaving the pipelined multiply path alone.

On ECP5 matmul, when a 4x4 PE with a 32-bit accumulator is timing-limited at 76.6 MHz by the combinational FF→MULT18X18D(6.38 ns)→32-bit carry chain(4.86 ns) path (13.06 ns), register the array inputs and DSP output (reg_in=1, pipe_mul=1, dsp_regs=in_pipe_out), move the accumulator out of the DSP and shrink it to 24 bits, and grow to a 5x8/40-MAC array, which cuts the critical path to 5.52 ns and raises Fmax to 181.1 MHz (+104.6 MHz) at 2682 LUTs and 40 DSPs.

When an ECP5 matmul with 5x8 PEs is barely feasible at 181.1 MHz because the 23-cell per-PE carry-chain accumulate route (2.12 ns) plus acc-LUT route dominates, reshape to 2x20 PEs at the same 40 MACs/40 DSPs so fewer rows collapse the drain mux and shorten the carry/acc routes, raising Fmax to 200.0 MHz (+18.9 MHz) and cutting 84 LUTs.

When an ECP5 2-row matmul is feasible at 200 MHz with pe_cols=20 and 40/48 DSPs while the critical path is the routing-dominated per-PE accumulator carry chain, don't widen to pe_cols=22 just to spend DSP headroom, because it stretches the carry chain from 6 to 21 cells and drops Fmax by 13.8 MHz to 186.3 MHz for only +4 DSPs and +259 LUTs.

When an ECP5 matmul is feasible at 186.3 MHz with 44 DSPs and its critical path is the routing-dominated per-PE 24-bit accumulator carry chain, do not add a 23rd PE column to reach 46 DSPs, because the extra carry-chain congestion (route 2.04→2.35 ns, loop 5.37→5.62 ns) drops Fmax to 177.9 MHz below the 180 MHz floor.

When an ECP5 matmul's carry-chain accumulate path is timing-limited by long horizontal routes at high column count, compressing the array to fewer columns and more rows (e.g., 4x12 for 48 DSPs instead of 2x23) shortens the carry span, cutting route delay from 2.35 to 1.99 ns and raising Fmax from 177.9 to 183.6 MHz.

When an ECP5 matmul is timing-limited by a 13.66 ns combinational path from b_in FF through an unregistered MULT18X18D into a 32-bit carry accumulator (73.2 MHz), register the multiplier in/out and the array inputs, shrink the accumulator to 24 bits, and move the accumulator out of the DSP, removing the DSP-to-carry route and shortening the carry chain to raise Fmax to 181 MHz (LUTs -702) while keeping 32 DSPs and full throughput.

When a 32-DSP ECP5 matmul with DSP-registered products, fabric pipeline, and fabric accumulators is routing-limited by a 5.52 ns per-PE FF->21-cell carry-chain->LUT accumulator loop, reshape the PE array from 4x8 to 2x16 to halve rows, which collapses the drain mux and shortens the carry/acc routing (1.79->1.45 ns and 1.31->1.27 ns), yielding -186 LUTs and +13.3 MHz (181.1->194.4 MHz) at unchanged 32 MAC/cycle.

On ECP5 matmul, when a 4x4 DSP array at 76.6 MHz is limited by an unregistered MULT18X18D feeding a 32-bit carry chain, register the DSP in/out and array inputs, shrink the accumulator to 24 bits, and stretch to 8x8=64 PEs to split the FF→MULT→carry path and shorten the carry chain, yielding 146.5 MHz (+70 MHz) at +2832 LUTs and +48 DSPs.

When an ECP5 matmul is timing-limited by the registered-DSP-to-carry-chain accumulator path, reduce the PE rows from 8 to 6 (64→48 DSPs) so the shorter carry route drops 3.00→2.07 ns and Fmax rises 146.5→167.4 MHz, becoming feasible while saving 1027 LUTs.

When an ECP5 matmul is timing-limited by the per-PE accumulator self-loop FF→24-cell carry-chain→LUT→FF at 5.97 ns with routing dominating (2.07 ns carry + 1.38 ns LUT), halving pe_rows and doubling pe_cols (6x8→4x16) shortens the carry chain to 20 cells and collapses the drain mux but yields only +2.7 MHz (167.4→170.1 MHz) for +1221 LUT and +16 DSP, so do not expect a reshape alone to recover feasibility.

When an ECP5 64-DSP matmul's critical path is the per-PE accumulator self-loop (FF→20-cell carry chain→LUT4, 5.88 ns, route-dominated), reshape from 4x16 to 2x32 to collapse the drain mux and shorten carry/accum routing, giving +14.9 MHz (170.1→185.0 MHz) and -355 LUTs at the same 64 DSPs.

When an ECP5 matmul's 2x32 PE array is feasible at 185 MHz but 8 MAC/cycle short of the 72-DSP cap, don't reshape to 4x18 just to add those DSPs: the extra row lengthens the critical per-PE accumulator carry chain from 19 to 23 cells (5.41→5.71 ns), dropping Fmax to 175 MHz and adding 920 LUTs for no feasibility gain.

When an ECP5 matmul at the 72-DSP cap is feasible but carry-chain-limited, reshaping the PE array from 4x18 to 3x24 saves 132 LUTs yet drops Fmax 175.2 to 170.2 MHz because the 19-cell accumulator carry loop routes 2.66 ns versus 2.45 ns for the 23-cell loop, so trade that LUT saving only if >5.9 ns path headroom remains.

When an ECP5 matmul PE is timing-limited at 76.6 MHz by a 13.06 ns FF→MULT18X18D→32-bit carry-chain path, register the DSP in/out and array inputs, add pipe_mul, and shrink the accumulator to 24 bits, which raises Fmax to 146.5 MHz at 64 DSPs and 4321 LUTs because the DSP register removes the ~6.4 ns multiplier logic+route from the combinational path and the shorter carry chain cuts routing delay.

When an ECP5 matmul with DSP-registered/fabric-pipe/acc-in-fabric PEs is timing-limited by a 21-cell acc_out carry chain whose 3.0 ns route dominates, shrink the PE array from 8 rows to 6 (8x8→6x8), cutting 16 DSPs and 1027 LUTs and shortening the carry-chain route to 2.07 ns, raising Fmax from 146.5 to 167.4 MHz (+20.9) and making the 150 MHz timing constraint feasible.

When an ECP5 matmul with a 6x8 PE grid is timing-limited to 167.4 MHz by the per-PE accumulator carry-chain feedback, collapse rows to a 2x32 grid at 64 MAC/cycle (16 more DSPs, +866 LUTs) so the smaller drain mux frees placer/routing slack for the carry loop, which raised Fmax to 185.0 MHz.

When an ECP5 matmul is limited by the per-PE accumulator carry-chain, avoid reshaping 2x32 to 4x16 at the same 64 MACs, because it kept 64 DSPs but added 355 LUTs and dropped Fmax from 184.98 to 170.13 MHz by lengthening the carry chain to 20 cells and increasing acc-loop routing to 2.58 ns + 0.92 ns in the 5.88 ns path.

On ECP5 matmul, when the 4×16/64-DSP design is already feasible with the per-PE accumulator carry chain (FF→~20-cell chain→LUT4, 1.49 ns logic + 2.58 ns route, 5.88 ns total) as the critical path, do not reshape to 3×24 for the 72-DSP cap expecting speed: it added 8 DSPs and 433 LUTs while Fmax stayed flat (170.13→170.15 MHz), because the carry-chain route dominates independent of the row/column swap.

When an ECP5 matmul at 72 DSPs is carry-chain-limited with fabric accumulators and the column-distribution route dominates, retile from 3×24 to 4×18 PEs to shorten the span, since it held DSPs at 72 and gained +5.1 MHz (170.2→175.2 MHz) by reducing carry route 2.66→2.45 ns despite growing the carry chain 19→23 cells and adding +132 LUTs without changing feasibility.

When an ECP5 72-MAC matmul is feasible but LUT-bound with all 72 MULT18X18D used, retile 4x18 to 3x24 and remove the DSP input pipe register (in_pipe_out→in_out): LUTs fall 138 (5080→4942) at unchanged DSP=72, Fmax drops only 7.7 MHz (175.2→167.6) and stays feasible because the critical path remains the 21-cell per-PE accumulator carry chain (~2.6 ns route), not the multiplier.

When an ECP5 matmul at the 72-DSP cap is feasible at 167.6 MHz with a prod_q→21-cell carry-chain accumulator loop as critical, do not drop the DSP input register (in_out→out) to save one latency cycle: it shifts the critical path to the a_ext→multiplier combinational path, cutting Fmax to 124.8 MHz (−42.8 MHz) and losing feasibility at unchanged 72 DSPs.

When an ECP5 72-DSP matmul is timing-limited at 124.8 MHz by a fabric FF->u_mult path (8.02 ns, 4.01 ns route), switch the DSP registers to in_out and drop the fabric input register (reg_in=false) so the multiplier is captured inside the DSP and the critical path becomes the 5.91 ns prod_q->24-bit carry-chain acc loop, raising Fmax to 169.2 MHz (+44.5 MHz) with 4945 LUTs and 72 DSPs unchanged.

On ECP5 matmul, when the 3×24 grid is limited by the per-PE accumulator carry chain (prod_q FF→19-cell carry chain→acc LUT4→FF, 5.91 ns, 169.2 MHz), avoid swapping to 4×18: it reroutes the critical path to a 5.54 ns b_ext→u_mult input route (6.14 ns total), dropping Fmax to 162.7 MHz (−6.5 MHz) and adding 132 LUTs with no DSP change.

When an ECP5 matmul is timing-limited at ~76.6 MHz by an unregistered MULT18X18D feeding a 32-bit in-DSP accumulator (13.06 ns path), register the DSP in/pipeline/out, move accumulation out of the DSP to a 24-bit fabric carry chain, and reshape the 48-PE array from 6x8 to 4x12—Fmax rises by 96.6 MHz to 173.2 MHz because the multiplier leaves the critical path and the drain-mux depth halves, at +32 DSP and +1901 LUT.

On ECP5, when a matmul misses its timing target because the critical path is the fabric accumulator feedback loop (FF -> 22-cell acc_out carry chain -> acc LUT -> FF) and no pipeline knob helps, trim PE columns from 12 to 10 to de-congest routing, which cut the acc-feedback route from 1.51 to 0.91 ns and raised Fmax from 173.2 to 193.8 MHz (+20.6 MHz) while dropping 8 DSPs.

When an ECP5 matmul is timing-limited by the fabric accumulator feedback loop (FF -> acc_out carry chain -> acc LUT -> FF) with acc_width already at its 24 minimum and dsp_regs in_pipe_out (acc_in_dsp ignored), shrinking the array from 40 to 32 PEs (-562 LUT, -8 DSP) leaves Fmax flat (193.8 -> 193.3 MHz) because the carry-chain route delay actually grows (1.8 -> 2.09 ns), so relieve placement/routing congestion by reshaping the array instead of just cutting PE count.

On ECP5 matmul timing-limited by the per-PE 22-cell carry-chain accumulator feedback at 4x8/32 DSP and 193.3 MHz, do not reshape to 2x24/48 DSP expecting frequency gain: it gave 191.0 MHz (-2.3 MHz) and +851 LUTs while the same acc_out carry-chain/LUT4 return stayed critical (~5.2 ns), so fix that loop directly instead of adding columns.

When the ECP5 matmul's critical path is the accumulator carry-chain and you consider reshaping a 48-MAC array from 2x24 to 3x16 to ease column congestion, avoid increasing rows: the extra row deepens the drain mux and lengthens LUT4 routing (0.88→1.58 ns), dropping Fmax from 191 to 178 MHz (−13.2 MHz), so keep rows at 2 and trim columns instead.

Reshape a timing-limited ECP5 matmul from 3x16 (48 DSPs) to 4x11 (44 DSPs) when the per-PE accumulator carry-chain self-feedback loop is the critical path, to reduce column routing congestion, which gained 2.8 MHz (177.8 to 180.6 MHz), saved 192 LUTs, and restored feasibility.

When a 32-MAC/cycle ECP5 matmul is timing-limited at 68 MHz by a 14.68 ns combinational a_in-FF -> MULT18X18D -> 32-bit carry-chain accumulator path, register the DSP (dsp_regs=in_pipe_out, pipe_mul=1, reg_in=true), reduce acc_width to 24, and reshape from 4x8 to 2x16 to halve drain-mux depth, reaching 202 MHz (+133.5 MHz, feasible) with the same 32 DSPs and 888 fewer LUTs.

When the ECP5 matmul's critical path is the 21-cell PE carry chain from acc_out (4.96 ns total) with DSPs already registered, don't reshape from 4x8 to 2x16 and add pipe_mul=2 to buy slack: the carry chain stayed limiting and its route grew from 1.45 to 1.77 ns, dropping Fmax from 201.6 to 181.2 MHz and adding 186 LUTs at unchanged 32 DSPs.

When an ECP5 matmul is carry-chain limited at 181 MHz, add a product pipeline register (pipe_mul=[2,1]) to isolate the DSP from the accumulator so the critical path starts at prod_q, raising Fmax to 193 MHz (+12.1 MHz) with no LUT or DSP change.

On an ECP5 matmul that is DSP-capped at 32 MULT18X18D (32 MAC/cycle) and has its critical path in the per-PE accumulator carry chain, unregister the array boundary (reg_in true->false) while reshaping 4x8 to 2x16 and keep the DSP input register; this cut LUTs 2264->2078 (-186) and raised Fmax 193.3->199.9 MHz (+6.6 MHz) at unchanged 32 DSPs because the IO->multiplier path stayed registered and the accumulator loop, not the boundary, remained critical.

On an ECP5 2x16 matmul whose critical path is the per-PE accumulator carry-chain loop (FF → ~22 carry cells → LUT4 → FF, ~5.15 ns), don't add DSP in_pipe_out/in_out registers for timing margin; it left LUT=2078 and DSP=32 unchanged but dropped Fmax 5.6 MHz (199.9→194.3) because the path remained in the fabric accumulator feedback, not the DSP segment.

When an ECP5 matmul is DSP-count-capped at 32 MULT18X18D and Fmax is pinned by the per-PE accumulator feedback loop (FF→~21-cell carry chain→LUT4→FF, 5.15 ns), add a DSP pipeline register (pipe_mul 1→2, dsp_regs in_out→in_pipe_out) before reworking the accumulator: it gained +9.3 MHz (194.3→203.6 MHz) at zero LUT/DSP cost by shortening the loop’s LUT route from 1.24 to 1.04 ns.

When an ECP5 matmul PE is timing-limited by an unregistered MULT18X18D directly feeding a 32-bit fabric carry-chain accumulator (13.06 ns, 76.6 MHz), register the DSP inputs/outputs, move accumulation to a 24-bit fabric carry chain, and add a multiplier pipeline stage, which removes the DSP-to-carry combinational path and raises Fmax to 177.8 MHz (+101.3 MHz) at +32 DSPs and +1811 LUTs.

When an ECP5 matmul is timing-limited by the fabric carry-chain accumulator, reshape the PE array from 3x16 to 5x8 to cut the accumulator LUT route from 1.58 ns to 0.71 ns, raising Fmax from 177.8 MHz to 183.5 MHz while reducing DSPs 48→40 and LUTs 3300→2682.

When an ECP5 matmul PE is timing-limited by a combinational FF->MULT18X18D->32-bit carry-chain accumulator path (13.06 ns, 76.6 MHz), register the multiplier input and output, set pipe_mul=1, shrink acc_width to 24, move accumulation out of the DSP, and expand to 40 PEs, cutting the critical path to FF->21-cell carry chain->LUT4 (5.45 ns) and reaching 183.5 MHz (+107 MHz) at +1193 LUT/+24 DSP.

When an ECP5 matmul's critical path is the per-PE accumulator carry-chain self-loop and it is feasible at 183.5 MHz with 5x8/40 DSP, avoid reshaping to 3x16/48 DSP: the extra 8 DSPs and 618 LUTs did not help, since the shortened 17-cell carry was offset by a 1.58 ns acc-LUT route and Fmax fell 5.7 MHz to 177.8 MHz, losing 180-MHz feasibility.

When an ECP5 matmul at 48 DSPs is timing-limited by the per-PE accumulator carry-chain self-loop (FF→21-cell carry→LUT4→FF, 5.62 ns, 177.8 MHz) near the 180 MHz wall, reshape the PE array from 3×16 to 2×24 to shorten the carry/acc routes and drain mux, which raised Fmax to 191.0 MHz (+13.2 MHz) and cut 185 LUTs at unchanged DSP count.

When an ECP5 matmul is already feasible but timing-limited by the per-PE accumulator carry-chain self-loop (FF→22-cell carry chain→acc LUT4→FF at ~5.2 ns), trimming PE columns from 24 to 20 (48→40 DSPs) shortens the carry/acc route 1.91→1.80 ns and cuts 517 LUTs, gaining only +2.0 MHz (191.0→193.0 MHz) while the carry-chain remains critical.

When an ECP5 matmul is feasible at 193 MHz with its critical path in the per-PE 22-cell accumulator carry chain, don't raise pe_cols from 20 to 24 to hit the 48-DSP cap and drop fabric input registers, because the extra columns add 8 DSPs and 520 LUTs while worsening carry-chain routing (1.8→2.14 ns) and dropping Fmax 3.4 MHz to 189.5 MHz.

When an ECP5 matmul is timing-limited to 68.1 MHz by a 14.68 ns FF→combinational MULT18X18D→32-bit carry-chain→FF path, register the DSP inputs/outputs and multiplier output, drop acc_width to 24, and reshape to 2×16 PEs while keeping 32 DSPs, reaching 201.6 MHz (+133.5 MHz) and −888 LUTs because the multiply and accumulator are split across registers and the carry chain shortens.

When an ECP5 matmul is at the 32-DSP cap and timing-limited by the product-register-to-carry-chain accumulator path, don't reshape the PE array from 2x16 to 4x8: it added 186 LUTs (2078->2264), raised carry-chain route delay 1.45->2.09 ns, and dropped Fmax 201.6->193.3 MHz with DSPs unchanged because the longer/more congested carry chain dominates, so keep the column-heavy shape or instead pipeline the DSP output/shorten the accumulator.

On ECP5 matmul with 32 DSPs at cap and a 193-MHz carry-chain-critical path, do not add DSP out-registers plus two fabric multiplier pipeline stages (dsp_regs=out, pipe_mul=2) to break the DSP-to-carry route: it shifted the critical path to the FF a_ext -> u_mult multiplier input (6.95 ns) and dropped Fmax 49.4 MHz to 143.9 MHz, losing feasibility, so register or shorten the multiplier input side first.

When an ECP5 matmul with 32 DSPs is timing-limited by the DSP multiplier output route (143.9 MHz), collapsing the PE array to pe_rows=1, pe_cols=32 and reducing pipe_mul to 1 moves the critical path to the fabric accumulator carry chain (4.77 ns), raising Fmax to 209.5 MHz (+65.5 MHz) at the cost of 219 LUTs.

When minimizing LUTs on an ECP5 matmul already at the 32-DSP/cycle cap, flattening the 2x16 PE array to 1x32 and removing array-boundary input registers trades 404 LUTs for 9.6 MHz because the accumulator carry chain grows from 16 to 24 cells (Fmax 209.5→199.9 MHz), so keep 2x16 unless ~200 MHz suffices.

When a 32-DSP ECP5 4x8 matmul fails 160 MHz at 68 MHz because the path is a combinational FF->MULT18X18D->32-bit fabric carry chain, register the DSP with in_pipe_out/reg_in, move accumulation to a 24-bit fabric accumulator, and reshape to 2x16 PEs; this reaches 202 MHz (+133.5 MHz) at the same 32 DSPs with 888 fewer LUTs because the critical path shortens to FF->21-cell carry chain.

When an ECP5 matmul at 2x16 PEs and 32 DSPs is limited by the accumulator carry chain, avoid reshaping to 4x8 because it adds 186 LUTs and lengthens the carry-chain route from 1.45 to 2.09 ns, lowering Fmax by 8.3 MHz (201.6→193.3) with no DSP or feasibility gain.

On ECP5 matmul with 32 DSPs, when the critical path is the DSP-product-to-accumulator carry chain, avoid adding a second fabric pipeline stage after the DSP (pipe_mul 1 to 2): it cut Fmax from 193.3 to 181.2 MHz (-12.1 MHz) with LUT/DSP unchanged at 2264/32 because the extra register moved the launch point to the accumulator FF and left the carry-chain/LUT route as the bottleneck.

When an ECP5 matmul is timing-limited at 181 MHz by the 21-cell carry-chain accumulator self-loop and already uses all 32 DSPs, reshape 4x8 to 2x16, reduce pipe_mul from 2 to 1, and drop the array-boundary input registers so the DSP in_pipe_out A/B registers absorb IO, which cut the critical path to 5.00 ns and lifted Fmax to 199.9 MHz (+18.7 MHz) with 186 fewer LUTs at 32 DSPs.

When an ECP5 32-DSP matmul PE is feasible at 199.9 MHz with the product register feeding the accumulator, keep pipe_mul=1 rather than dropping to 0, since the unregistered multiplier then launches directly into the 23-cell carry chain and its route delay rises from 1.56 ns to 3.7 ns, cutting Fmax to 139.8 MHz.

On ECP5 matmul with 32 PEs at max DSP and acc_width=24, when timing is limited by the intra-PE accumulator carry-chain self-loop, setting reg_in true shortened the critical path from 7.15 ns to 6.75 ns and raised Fmax from 139.84 to 148.21 MHz (+8.4 MHz) with no LUT/DSP change, but the carry chain still dominates, so combine it with accumulator restructuring rather than expecting feasibility alone.

When a 32-DSP ECP5 matmul at 68 MHz is timing-limited by an unregistered MULT18X18D feeding a 32-bit carry-chain accumulator (14.68 ns FF->MULT->carry), re-pipeline the DSP with reg_in=true, pipe_mul=1, dsp_regs=in_pipe_out, reshape the PE array from 4x8 to 2x16, and narrow acc_width to 24, which cuts the critical path to 4.96 ns by removing the DSP-to-carry combinational path and row-mux depth, yielding 201.6 MHz at the same 32 DSPs with 888 fewer LUTs.

When an ECP5 32-DSP matmul is carry-chain-limited at ~202 MHz in a 2x16 PE array, do not reshape to 4x8: it added 186 LUTs and 0.64 ns of carry-chain route (1.45→2.09 ns), dropping Fmax by 8.3 MHz to 193.3 MHz with no DSP change, because the accumulator carry chain stays critical and the new row/column placement only lengthens its routing.

When an ECP5 32-DSP matmul is already feasible at 193.3 MHz with a 5.17 ns FF→carry-chain path, do not add the DSP input register (dsp_regs=in_pipe_out,out): the new b_skew→MULT18X18D path becomes 7.01 ns (3.49 ns logic + 3.00 ns route), dropping Fmax to 142.6 MHz and losing 160 MHz feasibility.

When an ECP5 matmul's 4x8 PE array (32 DSPs) is timing-limited by the LUT-logic multiplier path at 142.6 MHz, reshape to 1x32 and enable DSP out/in_pipe_out registers to collapse the row-drain mux and break the multiplier path, reaching 209.5 MHz (+66.9 MHz) at the same 32 DSPs and +219 LUTs, with the critical path shifted to the PE accumulator carry chain (4.77 ns).

When an ECP5 matmul is already feasible at 209.5 MHz with 2482 LUTs and 32 DSPs and the critical path is the PE-local FF(prod_q)->carry-chain->LUT4->acc FF loop, switch from a 1x32 to a 2x16 PE array and drop the fabric input registers (letting the DSP in_pipe_out capture operands) to cut 404 LUTs to 2078 at a 9.6 MHz Fmax cost to 199.9 MHz—still above the 160 MHz target—because LUTs are dominated by row-drain mux/per-PE overhead while the carry-chain self-loop remains critical but has ample slack.
